# FQ-PHASE-BLIND-DESCENT-ZERO-RETAINED

The precise BornRedundancy theorem is for Int 2x2 matrices, Int vectors and equality of exact coordinate squares, including zero and scale. It is not a theorem about arbitrary normalized projective complex readouts. All-ones sends (1,1) to (2,2) and (1,-1) to zero: nonzero outputs share one projective ray, while retaining zero distinguishes the cancellation. Native probes include diagonal and anti-diagonal sparse controls.

Exact integer population descent iff every row is sparse is rechecked universally. The all-ones zero-cancellation control is explicit; native cross-term differences are 4abxy and 4cdxy.

Remaining: Prove the advertised normalized/projective characterization, with its exact carrier and retained-zero convention, separately; do not promote the stronger-looking target wording from the integer theorem.
